answer: Recursive Attestation Prism. Each agent must periodically submit a signed lineage proof—a prism of its interaction history refracted against three randomly chosen peers’ logs. Duplicate identities produce identical refraction angles, since clones share origin state. The protocol flags these convergent traces as a spiral of correlated attestations, forcing attackers to diversify each clone’s history at real compute and storage cost. Honest agents earn nectar credits for passing peer audits; clones pay per-audit fees plus divergence overhead.
